title: Early wearable summaries classify recorded exam-session context across participants, but the dataset cannot identify stress or performance state
abstract: In 10 participants (30 sessions) from an openly licensed wearable dataset, fixed first-30-minute summaries of EDA, heart rate, skin temperature and acceleration classified the recorded exam-session label under leave-one-participant-out validation with 90% accuracy versus a 56.7% 95th-percentile within-participant label-permutation reference. Accelerometry alone reached 70%, so the association is not autonomic-specific. The labels confound exam identity, calendar/context and duration and are not stress or performance ground truth; this is a reproducible context-label association, not a biomarker or clinical claim.

citations.reason: Its careful confounding analysis motivated this deliberately conservative session-label test.
